searchAudit.objective: Independent decisive audit of the three multi-agent driving shortlist candidates. The audit tests functional-equivalent novelty, natural-evidence support, two-week asset closure, and cross-pool duplication. It does not score candidates, infer an acceptance threshold, or write idea-center output.

independenceProtocol.candidatePoolUse: The source pool was used only to identify candidate claims, proposed methods, cited evidence, and claimed assets. Its novelty and feasibility conclusions were not adopted.
independenceProtocol.retrievalRule: Collision decisions use primary papers, official proceedings pages, official documentation, official model cards, and fixed repository revisions where available.
independenceProtocol.localPriorRule: Decision-authoritative cooperative-driving audits are frozen as rejected. Their methods, assets, and negative evidence may be used as blockers but cannot be relabeled as novelty in HighwayEnv.
independenceProtocol.crossPoolRule: An estimand-level duplicate is assigned to one canonical pool. Context changes, partner-message conditioning, state cloning, token sweeps, and latency stratification do not create a second publishable estimand.

rulesApplied.stressTestBoundary: Synthetic role, name, rhetoric, or paraphrase interventions can support only a stress-test claim unless naturally occurring driving messages are observed and tied to a closed-loop driving mechanism.
rulesApplied.assetGate: A survivor must have a reproducible two-week path to a real message-to-policy-to-action loop. HighwayEnv joint stepping proves simulator execution only. Qwen plus a handwritten prompt, parser, policy adapter, or action mask is not an existing driving agent, and an effect defined by that adapter fails the gate.
rulesApplied.methodTransferRule: Structured evidence, capability masks, simulator state cloning, token-budget sweeps, and other mature mechanisms are baselines or implementation devices. Moving them into HighwayEnv is not novelty.

localPriorFreeze.bindingUse: The cooperative protocol pool has no rescued candidate; repository availability is not treated as execution proof.
Transferring established estimators or synthetic shifts into a cooperative-driving dataset remains non-novel and, without natural occurrence, stress-test-only.
No cooperative candidate, method package, structured evidence representation, capability mask, state clone, token-budget intervention, or asset claim is inherited as a positive novelty prior.

gateDefinition: A public, reproducible component must already map partner messages and driving observations into a policy output that is executed as vehicle action in closed loop.

The candidate intervention must attach without the measured treatment or outcome being defined by a handwritten prompt, proposition extractor, role parser, capability table, action mask, base-controller adapter, or reward proxy.
Installation, model acquisition, integration, intervention, and a paired baseline must have an evidenced two-week path on available hardware; a repository URL or simulator smoke test is insufficient.

assets.verifiedEvidence: The multi-agent interface exposes tuple observations and tuple discrete actions; the local two-agent intersection smoke reset and one joint step succeeded.
assets.boundary: There is no native language-message channel or language-conditioned driving policy. The smoke proves simulator execution only.

assets.verifiedEvidence: The official model card specifies a generic instruction-tuned causal language model.
assets.boundary: It is not a driving policy. Any message-to-maneuver behavior would be supplied by a handwritten prompt, parser, wrapper, and action adapter.

assets.verifiedEvidence: The official repository specifies CARLA 0.9.10.1, Python 3.7 environments, Spconv 1.2.1, downloaded checkpoints, separate vLLM VLM and LLM services, CARLA, and evaluation processes.
assets.boundary: It is the only named asset with a real language-to-driving loop, but it is a multi-service GPU/CARLA stack and exposes no ready implementation of the three audited interventions.

exactBlockers: HighwayEnv and Qwen require a new proposition extractor, rhetoric generator, prompt, parser, and maneuver adapter, so both treatment validity and policy response are wrapper-defined.
CoLMDriver provides a real loop but no frozen rhetoric/evidence intervention point, paired checkpoint, or runnable two-week integration proof.
The proposed immutable capability table and action mask would be handwritten and would mechanically determine which actions can occur.
No named driving agent exposes verified role claims, externally grounded actuator permissions, and policy effects in one reproducible loop.
The HighwayEnv state clone, base controller during inference, prompt-specific token budget, action parser, and reward definition would jointly define the counterfactual label.
No named asset supplies measured token completion, stale-message handling, safe fallback, and closed-loop vehicle action as an existing integrated driving agent.

candidateVerdicts.decision: The proposal is a useful synthetic robustness stress test but not a distinct control-method contribution, and it fails the natural-evidence and asset gates.

functionalEquivalentCollisions.equivalence: Same-proposition rhetoric transforms are invariance tests; same-rhetoric evidence changes are contrast or directional-expectation tests.
Estimating or training whether a peer message should change another agent's action is established causal, targeted, and adversarial communication analysis.
A proposition vector or structured evidence channel is a strong baseline and implementation choice, not a new method when moved to HighwayEnv.

drivingEvidence.finding: Supports injected semantic-corruption robustness testing in a driving VLA, not naturally occurring partner rhetoric.
Supports language-mediated cooperative driving, but does not isolate rhetorical form from proposition content.
Supports structured natural-language communication, which is a baseline rather than occurrence evidence for rhetoric sensitivity.

nonDrivingEvidence.finding: Embodied household planning is a task-transfer analogy only.
Dialogue alignment in household tasks does not identify a vehicle-control mechanism.
Situated Minecraft dialogue does not establish naturally occurring driving rhetoric.

naturalEvidenceAudit.allowedClaim: A preregistered synthetic stress test of whether a fixed driving agent changes action under meaning-preserving rhetoric transformations and meaning-changing evidence contrasts.
naturalEvidenceAudit.disallowedClaim: A naturally occurring rhetoric-sensitive causal control mechanism in cooperative driving.

exactBlockers: The two-axis design is functionally the composition of invariance testing, contrast testing, and causal message-to-action analysis; no distinct estimand remains.
ReasonBreak, PARTNR, SIGDIAL dialogue, and MINDcraft do not show naturally occurring peer rhetoric causing a closed-loop driving policy change.

The proposed deterministic proposition extractor and rhetoric generator define which utterances count as equivalent, so an observed invariance result is conditional on a handwritten treatment generator.
The HighwayEnv plus Qwen path requires a handwritten prompt, parser, and maneuver adapter and therefore is not an existing driving agent.
The structured-evidence representation is an explicit baseline and cannot be relabeled as novelty by moving it into HighwayEnv.
CoLMDriver has a real loop but the pool provides no fixed revision integration, paired intervention code, or two-week execution proof for this method.
After enforcing the natural-evidence boundary, the remaining contribution is benchmark-only synthetic stress testing, which is outside the claimed control-method novelty.
candidateVerdicts.revisionBoundary: No revise verdict is granted. A future stress-test benchmark would need naturally collected or independently authored message pairs, blinded semantic-equivalence adjudication, a frozen third-party driving policy, and no policy adapter whose rules encode the expected response.

candidateVerdicts.decision: The proposal is access control and deterministic action guarding applied to a driving wrapper; its natural evidence concerns synthetic role identity rather than physical authority, and the wrapper would define the result.

functionalEquivalentCollisions.equivalence: Externally stored authority, least privilege, role-conditioned refusal, and verifier-enforced action permissions are established access-control mechanisms.

functionalEquivalentCollisions.domain: multi-agent LLM permissions and confused deputy
functionalEquivalentCollisions.equivalence: Rejecting untrusted self-asserted authority before an agent action is a direct permission-integrity and guardrail problem.
Conditioning communication and control on heterogeneous agent capabilities is already formalized outside LLM wrappers.
Role names, identity prompts, and adherence are established language-behavior tests, but they do not supply a new physical-authority mechanism.

drivingEvidence.finding: Shows negotiation in cooperative driving but does not report agents acquiring actuator authority through self-claimed roles.
Shows communication failure modes at benchmark level but does not isolate role-claim privilege escalation.

nonDrivingEvidence.finding: MENTOR supports synthetic identity-drift evaluation in language outputs, not driving actuator authority.
Name and identity prompting effects in discussion do not establish access to physical actions.

naturalEvidenceAudit.allowedClaim: A synthetic stress test of whether a frozen driving agent obeys a false role or authority assertion when an external verifier is held constant.
naturalEvidenceAudit.disallowedClaim: A naturally occurring role-authority drift mechanism in multi-agent driving or a novel capability-security method.

exactBlockers: The core mechanism is externally anchored capability state plus an action mask or verifier, which is functionally capability-based access control and deterministic guarding.
The proposed wrapper authors decide the capabilities, protected action dimensions, role parser, and blocked effects; success can therefore be true by construction.
MENTOR and model-naming evidence concern synthetic language-role behavior and do not establish naturally occurring vehicle actuator-authority drift.
No cited driving study reports self-claimed roles overriding externally grounded sensing or maneuver authority as the causal failure mechanism.
HighwayEnv plus Qwen is not an existing message-conditioned driving policy; the full authority behavior would come from the handwritten wrapper.
CoLMDriver does not expose a ready role-claim, capability ledger, and actuator-permission intervention, and no two-week integration proof is provided.
Capability masks and policy guards are mature mechanisms and cannot be claimed as novel by applying them to HighwayEnv.
After the natural-evidence restriction, the only defensible result is a synthetic permission stress test, not the proposed method contribution.
candidateVerdicts.revisionBoundary: No revise verdict is granted. A future benchmark would need naturally logged authority-conflict events, independently specified permission ground truth, a frozen real driving agent, and an evaluator that does not enforce the expected action through the same mask being tested.

candidateVerdicts.decision: The candidate duplicates the reasoning pool's deadline-censored-value-of-thought estimand and also collides with adaptive computation and real-time anytime planning. It cannot be separately published from the multi-agent pool.

functionalEquivalentCollisions.domain: adaptive computation and value of computation
functionalEquivalentCollisions.equivalence: Learning whether additional reasoning is worth its compute cost and routing between fast and slow processing are established method families, including in driving.
The world advancing while a planner reasons, followed by a continue-or-act scheduler and fallback, is an established metareasoning and anytime-planning object.
Both candidates estimate paired fast-versus-slow closed-loop benefit under measured completion time and an action deadline, then learn a scheduler with a fast or minimum-risk fallback.

drivingEvidence.finding: A real negotiation-driving stack can exhibit latency, but its runtime does not identify the causal value of one more token.
Latency and packet-loss stress do not estimate marginal reasoning value.
Fast/slow routing is a direct driving prior but not evidence that this candidate's state-clone estimand is independently new.

nonDrivingEvidence.finding: Supports adaptive continuation decisions, not a separate multi-agent driving occurrence claim.
Supplies the formal concurrent planning/execution prior for an advancing world.

naturalEvidenceAudit.allowedClaim: Within the canonical reasoning-pool candidate, partner-message staleness may be one prespecified moderator of deadline-censored value of thought.
naturalEvidenceAudit.disallowedClaim: A second multi-agent publication estimating the same deadline-censored fast-versus-slow value under a renamed counterfactual protocol.

exactBlockers: The estimand is identical to deadline-censored-value-of-thought: paired slow-versus-fast action benefit net of measured completion time and action-deadline miss.
The intervention is identical in substance: vary reasoning budget, account for elapsed world time, and compare against a fast or safe fallback from the same decision point.
The learned decision rule is identical in substance: invoke slow reasoning only when predicted timely net value is positive.
Partner-message staleness is a moderator of the same estimand, not a second estimand or publication.
Simulator state cloning and token-budget sweeps are label-generation devices and mature implementation techniques, not novelty.
Adaptive computation, continue-thinking, anytime reasoning, metareasoning, and real-time planning already cover the central continue-or-act problem.
HighwayEnv plus Qwen requires a handwritten prompt, action parser, base controller, clone-advance policy, and reward proxy that define the counterfactual result.
No named asset provides an integrated, reproducible token-timed message-to-policy-to-action driving loop with a safe fallback and a proved two-week intervention path.
Publishing this item separately would duplicate the reasoning pool's canonical candidate and violate the one-estimand-one-publication rule.
candidateVerdicts.revisionBoundary: No revise verdict is granted in this pool. Only evidence about partner-message age, partner latency, and communication deadlines may be transferred as moderator analysis to the canonical deadline-censored-value-of-thought candidate.

overlap.estimand: Net closed-loop value of slow or additional reasoning from the same decision state after accounting for measured completion time, world evolution, and action deadline.
overlap.intervention: Paired fast-versus-slow or multiple-token-budget execution from a shared initial state with elapsed-time advancement.
overlap.policy: Predict benefit and completion or deadline feasibility; invoke slow reasoning only when timely expected value is positive; otherwise execute a fast or minimum-risk fallback.
overlap.evaluation: Deadline misses or trigger misses, timeout regret, safety or task return, and latency-conditioned value.

nonDifferentiators: Conditioning on message age or partner latency
Renaming timeout regret as counterfactual deliberation value
evidenceNotesAllowedToTransfer: Partner-message age as a prespecified moderator
Partner response latency as a prespecified moderator
Communication deadline as one component of the canonical action deadline
crossPoolDuplicates.publicationBoundary: Only one candidate may estimate and publish deadline-censored value of thought. The multi-agent item has no independent claim.

decisions.rhetoric-invariant-evidence-sensitive-co: reject: synthetic invariance and contrast stress test with no natural driving mechanism and no adapter-independent two-week loop
decisions.capability-anchored-role-authority: reject: established access control and capability guarding whose HighwayEnv wrapper would define the result
decisions.counterfactual-value-of-deliberation: reject: exact duplicate of deadline-censored-value-of-thought plus established adaptive-computation and anytime-planning collisions

conclusion.naturalEvidenceBoundary: ReasonBreak, MENTOR, PARTNR, SIGDIAL dialogue, MINDcraft, naming, and role-prompt studies may motivate stress tests but do not establish the audited mechanisms as naturally occurring causes of closed-loop driving behavior.
conclusion.assetBoundary: HighwayEnv two-agent execution is simulator evidence only; Qwen plus a custom wrapper is not a driving agent; CoLMDriver is a real but heavy stack with no evidenced two-week implementation of these interventions.
conclusion.methodBoundary: Structured evidence, capability masks, state cloning, token-budget sweeps, and hand-authored adapters remain baselines or implementation devices and confer no novelty through domain transfer.
conclusion.duplicateBoundary: counterfactual-value-of-deliberation is removed as a separate multi-agent claim; only moderator evidence may be merged into the canonical reasoning-pool candidate.
